report.clinical_summary: Patient with HIV reports persistent headaches (2-3x/week, 7-8/10 intensity) and low-grade fatigue that began shortly after starting current medication a year ago. They question whether the medication is helping with symptoms and have taken days off ('drug holidays') when feeling well, believing their body can cope without it. The illness has impacted work performance and relationships, and they experience ongoing worry about the future and potential side effects. They have limited understanding of how the medication works and actively seek clearer information.

evidence.quote: At work, there are times when I feel like I'm not performing as well as I used to because of this constant low-level exhaustion.
It's also been hard to maintain relationships — sometimes people just don't understand what it’s like to live with a chronic condition like this.

The headaches have been happening every few days, maybe two or three times a week. They're not constant but when they hit, they can be quite intense. I would say they are around 7-8 out of 10 in terms of pain level.

As for the fatigue, it's been more of a low-grade feeling all the time. It's not like I can sleep all day, but I just feel that I have less energy than before. It doesn't really go away, so it makes getting through the day quite difficult at times.

consequences.reasoning: The patient has significant functional impairment - work performance is affected, relationships are strained, and they experience daily headaches (7-8/10) and persistent fatigue that makes daily tasks difficult. This is more than just adaptation - they've had to scale back their performance and struggle with maintaining relationships.

evidence.quote: The headaches began shortly after I started my current treatment about a year ago.
But then again, since this is a chronic condition, it feels like there's always going to be some level of struggle in managing it.
But like I said earlier, doctor, the uncertainty around all this is something I've learned to live with. I take things one day at a time and do what I can to keep myself as healthy as possible.
The idea of being on medicine every day for the rest of my life is definitely hard to wrap my head around.

timeline.reasoning: The patient clearly views HIV as a chronic, long-term condition that will require ongoing management. They've been on treatment for a year and expect to continue for the rest of their life. They acknowledge uncertainty but plan for the long term.

I take things one day at a time and do what I can to keep myself as healthy as possible.
